Resolves #19086

The dense Workstation control's dark-mode press landed on `<html>`: the theme toggle's view transition (`Workspace#toggleWorkspaceTheme` → `DomAccess.startViewTransition`, a 100 ms capture window plus a 500 ms reveal) owns hit-testing while it runs, so `:active` never reached the splitter and the drag never started. Both presses now wait until a hit test at the splitter's centre returns the splitter; the four hover/active colour reads wait for the splitter's 120 ms `background-color` transition; the tour monitor counts the tab containers' own header toolbars (each rail's reveal overlay composes a runtime-only one); duplicate-overflow samples name a control's real toolbar via `closest()`. Reaching the tour unmasked two reds that are not test premises — #19094 (a newborn split container flashes its overflow control for one frame, deterministic) and a Canvas receipt flake (defect-note, 09:14Z). The probe facts behind each layer are in #19086's Classification section.

Evidence: L2 (headless e2e over the seat's own Neural Link bridge, `NEO_NL_PORT` per #19066) → L2 required (AC-2 is an e2e receipt). Residual: AC-2's original whole-file 9/9, Residual-Owner: #19094.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the pre-commit lint-staged hooks ran (whitespace, shorthand, jsdoc-types, ticket-archaeology, block-alignment, parse, derived-domain, fixed-sleeps).

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | outside-CI: instrumented runs 08:48–08:52Z — `elementsFromPoint` at the press returned only `html`, the `::view-transition-*` animations stood at t = 100 ms, the splitter became hit-testable 394–415 ms later; recorded in #19086's Classification section |
| AC-2 | outside-CI: `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=<brain> NEO_NL_PORT=8093 npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNL.spec.mjs -g "the real tour keeps density"` — the dark arm's `:active` and active-vs-hover reads passed and the drag committed `resizeSplit` in 6 of 6 runs since the settled reads (08:58–09:13Z) |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: the light arm's `:active`, active-vs-hover and opacity asserts are unchanged and green in every run; whole file at `f8e64bf9fd`: 8 passed, 1 failed, the red after both arms |

## Deltas from ticket
- The dark arm keeps the UA `:active` read: the ticket's fallback (token reads) was written for a proxy taking the target; the target-taker is the theme reveal, so the read stays honest once the press lands.
- Both arms gain the precondition, not only the dark one — the light arm was shielded solely by its 1.2 s listener-readiness wait.
- The four colour reads settle on `getAnimations().length === 0` (a 1-in-3 flake that appeared once the press landed).
- The monitor's header scope and the exact overflow-owner attribution (the attribution is what let #19094 be filed with real owners).

## Test Evidence
- Whole file at `f8e64bf9fd` (rebased on `dev@9c5b5f9b7c`): 8 passed, 1 failed — the dense test at the Canvas receipt (`:1513`, the defect-noted flake, 5 of 9 runs today). In the runs that pass it, the next and only red is #19094's one-frame duplicate (3 of 3 runs that reached the monitor).
- Negative control: without the press precondition the dark arm reds identically on clean `dev` (three sightings in the ticket plus the first instrumented run); with it, the drag commits `resizeSplit` (`sizes[0]` delta > 0.02) every run.
- Falsified: a 400 ms held press without movement does not stop the sparklines painting (four pulses repainted in 246–264 ms), so the Canvas flake is not the settled reads' doing.
- Not in CI: `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` is deselected by the e2e CI filter (Neural Link specs), so every receipt above is local.
